newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA WARNS NATO RISKS GREY AREA IN BALKANS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA WARNS NATO RISKS GREY AREA IN BALKANS.

text.p: Bulgaria has sought U.S. support for its application to join NATO, warning that by leaving it out the alliance risked creating a "grey area" in the Balkans, the presidency said on Thursday.
Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov said in a letter to U.S. President Bill Clinton that the development of NATO should reflect the development of Europe itself.

"And such development excludes the emergence of a 'grey area' in southeast Europe, which bears the risk that Bulgaria could turn from 'an island of stability' into 'an island of uncertain security'," the presidency quoted the letter as saying.
European security should be defined by the objective demands of the present and the future, not the tragedies of the past, said the letter.

Bulgaria's interim cabinet in February made a clear statement of their desire to join NATO, an issue on which the former Socialist government had always been ambivalent for fear of upsetting their traditional allies in Moscow.
NATO is due to issue formal membership invitations to former East Bloc states at a meeting in July.
